title: Quality Disclosures and Disappointment: Evidence from the Academy Awards
eligible_reason: Section 4 DiD (Table 3, Figure 4; RUN_DID.do lines 26-80) compares MovieLens ratings of AMPAS-nominated vs non-nominated movies in an 80-day window around each award year's nomination date (1995-2019). Each movie enters once, assigned to one award-year cohort (non-nominated films get a 'reference nomination date'), and the time FE are relative-day FE: reghdfe rating nominated after_nom treated, absorb(movieid diff_date_nom_ref), where diff_date_nom_ref is days relative to the movie's own (reference) nomination date (main_body.tex line 352: 'day fixed effects capture all variations in ratings posted on specific days relative to the nomination date'). after_nom is a post indicator for all movies at their cohort date (extra treatment regressor). This is a cohort-aligned (stacked-type) event-time design with clean controls per cohort and no calendar-time FE, so it is not an eligible design. Even with calendar-date FE the 80-day windows of different award years do not overlap, so date FE would equal cohort x relative-day FE and the design reduces to a stack of single-date DiDs with never-nominated controls (no staggered comparisons). The main results (Section 5) are user-level propensity-score matching on recommender embeddings (areg rating ATT, absorb(movieid)); Section 6 IMDb uses the same matching. Table D16 adds predicted ratings or embeddings as controls.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe/areg; Python recommender (LensKit, scikit). Table 3 cols 1-4: no FE; genre+year FE; movie FE; movie + relative-day FE. Figure 4: reghdfe rating i.nominated##ib13.diff_date_nom_5, absorb(movieid diff_date_nom_5) (5-day relative bins). Nomination dates: early February before 2004, mid-January since 2004, one date per year; cohorts aligned on event time.
main_or_robustness: main (DiD is the first-pass analysis; matching is the main estimate)

published_estimates.note: Nominated x post with movie and relative-day FE (from main_body.tex)

data_files_note: Raw MovieLens 25M, scraped IMDb data and AMPAS dates shipped; the processed did_characteristics.dta is not shipped but is built by RUN_cleaning.do.
screener_notes: Title from README/main_body.tex (not in candidates.csv). DiD uses relative-day FE with per-cohort controls (stacked-type), not calendar-time FE.
